# Copilot Instructions for frescopa-stage

This is an **Adobe Edge Delivery Services (EDS/Franklin) "Crosswalk" site** for AEM Authoring,
integrated with **Adobe Commerce** via `@dropins/*` storefront drop-in components. It is a fork of
`aem-showcase/frescopa` (itself based on `hlxsites/aem-boilerplate-commerce`), auto-synced hourly by
`.github/workflows/sync-upstream.yml`. `fstab.yaml` (author mountpoint) is intentionally preserved
from the fork during upstream merges — never let a sync overwrite it, and be aware that most other
files can be overwritten by the next scheduled sync.

## Build, lint, and test

- Install deps: `npm i` (this triggers `postinstall` → `install:dropins`, which copies drop-in
  packages from `node_modules/@dropins` into `scripts/__dropins__` and copies the Magento storefront
  event collector/SDK into `scripts/`). Re-run manually after touching any `@dropins/*` version:
  ```sh
  npm install @dropins/storefront-cart@x.y.z
  npm run postinstall
  ```
- Lint JS: `npm run lint:js` (ESLint, airbnb-base + `eslint-plugin-xwalk`). Lint CSS:
  `npm run lint:css` (stylelint-config-standard on `blocks/**/*.css` and `styles/*.css`). Both:
  `npm run lint`. Auto-fix: `npx eslint . --fix`.
- Local dev server: `npm start` (runs `aem up --print-index`, serves at `http://localhost:3000`).
- Rebuild the merged component JSON (definitions/models/filters) after editing files under
  `models/_component-*.json`: `npm run build:json` (or the individual
  `build:json:models` / `build:json:definitions` / `build:json:filters` scripts). These merge into
  the root `component-models.json`, `component-definition.json`, `component-filters.json` — do not
  hand-edit those merged root files directly.
- E2E tests (Cypress) live in `cypress/` as a **separate npm project**: `cd cypress && npm install`.
  Requires the site running locally first (`npm start` from repo root, served on
  `http://127.0.0.1:3000`). Run all: `npm run cypress:run`. Run a single spec:
  ```sh
  npx cypress run --config-file cypress.config.js --spec "src/tests/e2eTests/verifyGuestUserCheckout.spec.js"
  ```
  Interactive/single-test debugging: `npm run cypress:open`, then pick the spec in the Cypress UI.
  CI (`run-e2e-tests.yaml`) only runs these against `hlxsites/aem-boilerplate-commerce` upstream, and
  the tests target Adobe Commerce's demo backend — they may not be meaningful against this fork's
  content without adjustment.
- CI (`main.yaml`) runs `npm ci && npm run lint` on every push — no unit test step; linting is the
  main automated gate.

## Architecture

- **Page rendering pipeline**: `scripts/aem.js` (EDS core: block/section decoration, lazy/eager
  loading phases) is orchestrated by `scripts/scripts.js`, which loads header/footer, decorates
  blocks/sections, and calls `initializeDropins()` from `scripts/initializers/index.js`.
- **Drop-ins** (`scripts/initializers/{account,auth,cart,checkout,order,pdp}.js`): each wraps a
  `@dropins/storefront-*` package (copied into `scripts/__dropins__/`, gitignored — regenerated by
  `postinstall`), wiring Commerce GraphQL data into the page. `scripts/commerce.js` holds shared
  commerce helpers/history tracking; `scripts/commerce-events-sdk.js` /
  `commerce-events-collector.js` feed the Adobe Data Collection Layer (`scripts/acdl`).
- **Blocks** (`blocks/<name>/<name>.js` + `.css`): standard EDS blocks. Commerce-specific blocks are
  prefixed `commerce-*` (e.g. `commerce-cart`, `commerce-checkout`, `commerce-account-header`) and
  typically render/mount a `@dropins` UI container rather than building DOM manually.
- **Authoring models** (`blocks/<name>/_<name>.json` + top-level `models/_*.json`): each block that
  is authorable in AEM Crosswalk defines a `_<name>.json` with `definitions` (xwalk resource type +
  block model reference) and `models` (field schema for the AEM dialog). `npm run build:json` merges
  all these fragments into the single root `component-models.json` /
  `component-definition.json` / `component-filters.json` consumed by the AEM author UI — always edit
  the per-block/`models/` source files, then rebuild, never the merged root JSON.
- **Content mapping**: `fstab.yaml` maps the EDS mountpoint to the AEM author instance;
  `paths.json` maps AEM author content paths (`/content/frescopa/...`) to site-relative URLs/JSON
  endpoints (config, placeholders, metadata, locations). `helix-query.yaml` / `helix-sitemap.yaml`
  configure the Helix index and sitemap.
- **Environment config**: `scripts/configs.js` picks `dev`/`stage`/`prod` from the hostname (or a
  `sessionStorage` override in non-prod) and loads the matching `configs[-env].json` at the site
  root, which supplies Commerce endpoint URLs, etc.

## Conventions

- Lint config is strict airbnb-base with a few repo-specific overrides (see `.eslintrc.js`): unix
  linebreaks required, `console.warn/error/info/debug` allowed (`console.log` is not), unused args
  starting with `_` are allowed, ES module imports must include the `.js` extension.
  `.eslintignore` excludes generated/vendored code (`scripts/__dropins__`, `scripts/acdl`,
  `scripts/widgets`, `tools/*`, `cypress/`, all block/model JSON, `blocks/video/videojs/*`) — don't
  fight lint errors there.
- `.editorconfig`: 2-space indent for JS, 4-space for CSS.
- Commit/PR convention (`CONTRIBUTING.md`): reference the GitHub issue ID in commits/PRs (or tag
  `[trivial]`), and start PR titles with the issue ID.
- **PR description must include a preview URL**, or the `AEM Code Sync / aem-psi-check` status
  check fails with "Rejected: provide test url". Add a "URL for testing" section pointing at the
  AEM live preview for the PR's branch, using the pattern
  `https://<branch>--<repo>--<owner>.aem.page/` (owner = the account/org the branch was pushed
  from, e.g. a fork owner if you don't have push access to this repo). Since `.aem.page` hostnames
  are DNS labels, a trailing `-` in the owner name (e.g. GitHub handle `fe-lix-`) is dropped from
  the domain — use `https://fix-teaser-delivery-tier-image-link--frescopa-stage--fe-lix.aem.page/`,
  not `...--fe-lix-.aem.page/`. Verify the URL returns real HTML (`curl -I <url>`) before adding it
  to the PR description; the check re-runs its own Lighthouse pass against that exact URL on every
  new commit, so pushing a follow-up commit (e.g. an empty commit) after fixing the description
  re-triggers it.
